_notes: Rowamet Heavy Metal: the Taito do Brasil board with a Z80 as the main CPU and Rowamet's own sound board (PinMAME
machine rowamet, which imports the taito machine and its NVRAM handler). The firmware is Vortex's with a few
hundred bytes changed: the reset validation, the high-score and replay award code, the copy helpers and the ROM
defaults (same factory settings, same 600,000 high-score floor) are byte-identical, so this is vortex.map.json's
layout. Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the ROM code and a live capture on an AtGames ALP4K (Visual Pinball
Standalone): a one-player game read back 40,003 and two credits at a mid-game quit, with the tilt on ball 2
setting bit 1 of the flags byte and the games-played counter ticking at game start.
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The nine-byte BCD settings block is edited from the service menu and validated at reset (a non-BCD byte
restores all nine from ROM); its entries are named from the Shock (1979) and Cosmic (1981) operator sheets.
No checksum or mirror. The firmware deliberately resumes a game in progress at reset, so an image saved mid-game
holds that game: game_over clear and a ball in play.
Settings 05-07 (the replay levels and extra-ball score at 0x4074-0x4076) are not declared: this firmware
rebuilds all three from ROM, so a written value does not last. The routine (Mr. Black 0x026F; present in every
set listed) adds a BCD offset to the base at 0x1FF8-0x1FFA; the offset comes from the table at 0x1FD8, indexed
by the CODE 5-7 switches of the 'Adjust' DIP bank (input 0x2806, which PinMAME maps to DIP bank 0; CODE 5 is the
low bit). The Cosmic sheet says the same in its own words - 5o-7o 'only fixed values', 'automatically set from
the switches at every game start, no more manual adjustment' - and its eight CODE 5-7 levels (350K to 850K) are
Cosmic's base plus its table exactly. On Mr. Black it runs at reset, at each step of the attract cycle (0x03E9
into the settings validation, which ends in the call at 0x0192) and when a player is added (0x0861): levels
written in attract were back at 39/39/39 within six seconds, three times.
0x40F4-0x40FF holds the last game's final display (four scores, same encoding as 0x4080) once the game is over, while the attract alternates the live display between it and the high score.

Audits are 16-bit little-endian binary counters from +50, which the statistics display walks two bytes at a time (Vortex 0x08BB). Four are declared; +50, +58, +5A, +5E and +60 read zero in every capture, none of which included a credit award on this firmware.

player_count._notes: Read by the reset path, which refuses to resume a game with a value of 5 or more; 1 throughout a live one-player game, 0 in attract.
player_count.label: Players

current_player._notes: One bit per player - 1, 2, 4, 8 for players one to four, 0 in attract - which the values list turns into the player number. The firmware finds the number by rotating the byte right until the carry sets and compares it with the player count (0x0445, the same code as Vortex). Measured as 1 in a one-player game; 1, 2, 4, 8 were measured live in four-player games on Mr. Black, the same firmware family.
current_player.label: Current Player

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware keeps a display copy at 0x408D.
credits.label: Credits

match._notes: Match digit shown after the game; cycles 0-9 during play (the randomiser).
match.label: Match

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

tilted._notes: Bit 1 of the flags byte: set at a tilt on ball 2 and cleared when the next ball started (live).
tilted.label: Tilted

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.

01._notes: Labels and ranges from the Shock (1979) and Cosmic (1981) operator sheets; byte positions and defaults match every image captured. Defaults are each set's own factory table, read from its ROM (the ten bytes the reset path copies in when a settings byte is not BCD).
01.label: Balls Per Game

02._notes: 'Fichas/Partida' (Cosmic: 'Credito/Partida'). A two-digit code, not a count: the sheets allow 11-14 and list 15 as a forbidden value that forces the default. What the digits mean is not stated on either sheet.
02.label: Coinage (code)

03._notes: 'Credito/Maximo'. The firmware clamps the stored credits to this value at boot.
03.label: Maximum Credits

09._notes: 'Credito/Record': credits awarded for beating the high score. The Cosmic (1981) sheet allows 01 and 02; the Shock (1979) sheet 01 to 03.
09.label: Credits For High Score

01._notes: Ticks only while a game is running (live on Drakor and Oba-Oba), about every 64 s like the powered-on timer. The statistics display divides it by games played for an average game time.
01.label: Play Time (ticks)

02._notes: Ticks about every 64 s whether or not a game is running (Vortex in attract: 44, 108, 173, 237, 301 s).
02.label: Powered-On Time (ticks)

03._notes: One tick per coin, on the same poll the credit rose, in every live capture.
03.label: Coins

04._notes: Ticks at game start (live, one-player game). On Mr. Black, the same firmware family, it ticks once per player started.
04.label: Games Played
